hook.title: Two-in-One Words: Why Tildes Survive on -mente
hook.content: When you attach -mente to an adjective that already has a written accent mark — like rápida ('rapid') or fácil ('easy') — Spanish keeps that original written accent mark right where it was: rápidamente, fácilmente! Why? Because phonetically, -mente adverbs still have two stressed beats ('with a RAPID MIND')!

pattern.title: One Caveat: Actualmente
pattern.content: Remember our false-friend warning: mientras exactamente, perfectamente, totalmente, and naturalmente mean what they look like, actualmente means 'currently / at present' (never 'actually'!).

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: exactamente, naturalmente, perfectamente, totalmente, rápidamente, fácilmente
exercises.meaning: exactly, naturally, perfectly, totally, rapidly / quickly, easily
exercises.explanation: Adjectives with a tilde (rápida, fácil) keep their tilde when -mente is attached.

exercises.prompt: Build 'totally' in Spanish from the invariable adjective 'total':
exercises.explanation: Because total ends in a consonant (-l), it has no -a form — -mente glues directly onto total: totalmente.

exercises.prompt: Which spelling of 'quickly / rapidly' properly preserves the original adjective's accent mark?
exercises.explanation: rápida (feminine) + mente keeps the tilde on rá-: rápidamente.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: Lo comprendo totalmente — object pronoun before verb, adverb after verb.

summary.outcome: Build -mente adverbs from both -o/-a and invariable adjectives while preserving written tildes.

use_example.german: Lo comprendo perfectamente y hablo fácilmente.
use_example.english: I understand it perfectly and I speak easily.

summary.takeaway: Adjectives in -o flip to -a before -mente; invariable adjectives glue directly; tildes always survive.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([7] Questions: Inverted & Intonation): master Spanish question words and why they always wear an accent mark.

twist.explanation: Lo comprendo perfectamente places lo before comprendo.

exactamente.etymology_derivation: Latin ablative exactā mente ('with an exact mind') fused into a single adverb suffix.

naturalmente.etymology_derivation: natural + mente. When the adjective doesn't end in -o, it attaches directly.

rápidamente.etymology_derivation: rápida + mente. Keeps the accent on rá- even though the suffix is stressed.

actualmente.etymology_derivation: Latin actuālis ('pertaining to acts/now'). Spanish narrowed it to time ('currently'); English to reality ('actually' = en realidad).

mente.name: The -MENTE Adverb Engine
mente.phonetic_rule: Feminine adjective + -mente /-ˈmente/ forms adverbs corresponding to English -ly.
mente.historical_linguistics: Originates from the Latin ablative phrase [adjective] mente ('with a ... mind'). Because mens is feminine in Latin, Spanish preserves the feminine adjective stem.
mente.philological_note: Notice how Spanish preserves the feminine form: exactamente (not exactomente). If the base adjective carries a tilde, it keeps it: fácilmente.
